quests.instruction: The letter c says /k/ before a, o and u. Which word has the hard c sound?
quests.hint: Look at the letter that comes after the c.
quests.explanation: In “corn”, c comes before o, so it says /k/. In “city” and “cent”, c comes before i and e.
quests.funFact: C says /k/ before a, o and u, as in cat, cot and cup.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with /k/ spelled with the letter c?
quests.hint: Look for the word that starts with c and says /k/.
quests.explanation: “Cup” starts with c and says /k/. “Kit” also starts with /k/, but it uses k, and “cent” starts with /s/.

quests.instruction: Say “cap”, “cot” and “cut”. What sound does the c make?
quests.hint: Listen to the first sound in all three words.
quests.explanation: In “cap”, “cot” and “cut”, c comes before a, o and u, so it says /k/.

quests.instruction: When c comes before e, i or y, it often says /s/. Which word has the soft c sound?
quests.hint: Look at the letter after the c.
quests.explanation: In “city”, c comes before i and says /s/. In “cat” and “cot”, c says /k/.

quests.instruction: Which word spells its first sound /s/ with the letter c?
quests.hint: You need a word that begins with c, not s.
quests.explanation: “Circle” starts with /s/ spelled c. “Soup” starts with /s/ spelled s, and “carrot” starts with /k/.
quests.funFact: Soft c and soft g follow a similar pattern: they are usually soft before e, i and y.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? ni__ — kind and friendly.
quests.hint: Say the word. Which spelling makes the ending /s/?
quests.explanation: “Nice” ends with ce, where c is soft because it comes before e.

quests.instruction: Which word has the soft c sound?
quests.hint: Look at the letter after c in each word.
quests.explanation: In “face”, c comes before e, so it says /s/. In “fact”, c comes before t and says /k/.
quests.funFact: Face, race, nice, ice and place all end with a soft c followed by a silent e.

quests.instruction: Which word has the hard c sound?
quests.hint: Check which letter follows the c.
quests.explanation: In “candy”, c comes before a, so it says /k/. In “cell” and “city”, c says /s/.

quests.instruction: Which word has two c letters that make different sounds?
quests.hint: Say each word slowly and listen to each c.
quests.explanation: “Circus” has a soft c at the start and a hard c in the middle. “Cactus” has two hard c sounds, and “candy” has only one c.

quests.instruction: When g comes before e, i or y, it often says /j/. Which word has the soft g sound?
quests.hint: Look at the letter after the g.
quests.explanation: In “giant”, g comes before i and says /j/. In “goat” and “gum”, g says /g/.
quests.funFact: Soft g is the same sound as /j/ in jump.

quests.instruction: Which word has the hard g sound?
quests.hint: Check which letter follows the g.
quests.explanation: In “game”, g comes before a and says /g/. In “gem” and “gym”, g says /j/.

quests.instruction: Which word has a hard g and a short vowel?
quests.hint: Look at the letter after g, then check whether the vowel is short or long.
quests.explanation: “Gap” has a hard g and short a. “Gem” has a soft g, and “game” has a long a.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /j/ spelled ge?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen to the last sound.
quests.explanation: “Cage” ends with /j/ spelled ge. “Cake” ends with /k/ and “cap” ends with /p/.
quests.funFact: In words like cage, page and huge, the silent e lets the g say /j/.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? pa__ — you turn it when you read a book.
quests.hint: Say the word. Which letters make the ending /j/?
quests.explanation: “Page” ends with ge. We use ge after a long vowel sound like the a in page.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with the soft g sound?
quests.hint: Say the first sound of each word. Which one begins with /j/?
quests.explanation: “Giraffe” starts with /j/ spelled g before i. “Goat” and “gum” start with the hard /g/.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /j/ spelled dge?
quests.hint: Look at the last three letters.
quests.explanation: “Bridge” ends with dge.

quests.instruction: After a short vowel, /j/ is often spelled dge. Which word has a short vowel and ends with dge?
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel before the /j/. Is it short or long?
quests.explanation: “Badge” has short a and dge. “Page” has long a and ge, and “huge” has long u and ge.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? fu__ — a sweet chocolate treat.
quests.hint: Say the word. The vowel is short, so think of the longer spelling.
quests.explanation: “Fudge” has short u followed by dge.
quests.funFact: The d in dge is silent. It is just there to show that the vowel before it is short.

quests.instruction: Which letters spell the /k/ at the end of “back”?
quests.hint: Think about how many letters come after a short a.
quests.explanation: “Back” ends with ck after the short vowel a.
quests.funFact: The letters ck are never used at the start of an English word.

quests.instruction: Which letter spells /k/ at the start of “kitten”? Before e and i, we usually use k.
quests.hint: Look at the vowel after the first sound.
quests.explanation: “Kitten” starts with k because the vowel after it is i. A c before i would say /s/.

quests.instruction: Which word has /k/ spelled ck after a short vowel?
quests.hint: Check how each word ends.
quests.explanation: “Clock” has short o and ends with ck. “Cloak” has long o and ends with k, and “clip” ends with /p/.

quests.instruction: Which word has a different sound for the c than the others?
quests.hint: Look at the letter after the c in each word.
quests.explanation: In “cat” and “cup”, c says /k/. In “cell”, c comes before e and says /s/.
quests.funFact: Cell, city and cent all start with /s/ even though they begin with c.

quests.instruction: Which word has a different sound for the g than the others?
quests.hint: Look at the letter after the g in each word.
quests.explanation: In “gas” and “goat”, g says /g/. In “gem”, g comes before e and says /j/.

quests.instruction: Which pair starts with the same sound, even though the first letters are different?
quests.hint: Say each pair and listen to the first sound.
quests.explanation: “Cent” and “sent” both start with /s/. “Cat” and “can” start with /k/.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? e__ — the sharp side of a knife.
quests.hint: The vowel before the /j/ is short, so think of the longer spelling.
quests.explanation: “Edge” has a short e before the /j/, so it ends with dge.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /j/ sound at the start spelled with g?
quests.hint: You need a word that starts with g but says /j/.
quests.explanation: “Giant” starts with soft g. “Jump” spells /j/ with j, and “goat” has the hard /g/.
quests.funFact: Giant, gem and giraffe all begin with the /j/ sound, spelled with g.

quests.instruction: “Badge” ends with the long spelling dge. How many sounds does the whole word have?
quests.hint: Remember that dge makes one sound.
quests.explanation: “Badge” has 3 sounds: /b/ /a/ /j/. The letters dge together make a single /j/.

quests.instruction: Which word has a soft c?
quests.hint: Look at the letter after c.
quests.explanation: In “dance”, c comes before e and says /s/. In “camp” and “cold”, c says /k/.
quests.funFact: Dance, face and city all use a soft c.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /j/ sound spelled with g?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen for /j/.
quests.explanation: “Change” has /j/ spelled ge. “Chin” has /ch/ and “grab” has the hard /g/.

quests.instruction: Which word has a hard c and a soft g?
quests.hint: Check the c and the g separately.
quests.explanation: In “cage”, c comes before a and says /k/, and g comes before e and says /j/. “City” has a soft c and “gum” has a hard g.
